claims.harm: missing struct fields like best_height in estimateSmartFee and mismatched integer and enum types lead to serialization bugs and compilation issues
claims.quote: It seems to me the capnp wrapper needs some updates (missing field, 32/64 bit params, param rename, bool vs uint64, enums as unsigned, optional mapping, unused declarations, comments, etc).
claims.settled_by_quote: You found a lot of annoying discrepencies and a real bug in the estimateSmartFee best_height return value, which should all be fixed now.

claims.harm: node segfaults if a non-C++ client passes null transaction data or unhandled enum values over IPC
claims.quote: Also what happens here is tx is a null pointer (allowed by capnp spec AFAIU)? I think we will immediately try to deference it in BroadcastTransaction and segfault.

claims.harm: node aborts with an assertion failure if an IPC client requests getBlockHash for a height exceeding the active chain tip
claims.quote: when we pass the height, which is greater than the current tip, then the node crashes and exits with the error... Assertion `chainman().ActiveChain()[height]' failed. Aborted (core dumped)

support.reason: being able to work with any socket (TCP or UNIX) makes a lot of sense. you could have bitcoin-node on some secure computing host. and then one or more bitcoin-walet on over-the-network hosts.

tested ACK 395d5eed0475558de2c2a66914d5a5814ce38f3c. I've tested this with the Rust wallet PoC... exercises getHeight, getBlockHash, hasBlocks, findAncestorByHeight, findAncestorByHash, findCommonAncestor, initMessage, showProgress and handleNotifications. It also exercises all the ChainNotifications events.
implemented Rust bindings and an Electrs demo using IPC instead of RPC and P2P for block fetching, tx broadcast, tip updates, and mempool sync

Exposing interfaces::Chain over IPC seems very useful, especially for downstream users. I have been using a version of this branch myself on a node 'dashboard'... Long term, I think IPC should become the preferred integration boundary for programmatic interaction with Bitcoin Core.
